body_md:
We say that $f\in L^1(\Omega)$ belongs to $BV(\Omega)$ if there exists a vector valued measure
$Df=(D_1f,\ldots,D_kf)$ with finite total variation representing the derivative of $f$ in the sense of
distributions, namely
$$
\int_\Omega f\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x_i}\,dx=-\int_\Omega\phi\,dD_i f\qquad
\forall\phi\in C^\infty_c(\Omega),\,\,\,i=1,\ldots,k.
$$

title: Definition
body_md:
We say that ${\bf b}\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^k)$ belongs to $BD(\Omega)$ if there exists a symmetric matrix of measures
$E{\bf b}= (E{\bf b})_{ij}$, $1\leq i,j\leq k$, representing the symmetric part of the distributional derivative of ${\bf b}$, namely
$$
\frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega \bigl({\bf b}_i\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x_j}+{\bf b}_j\frac{\partial\phi}{\partial x_i}\bigr)\,dx=
-\int_\Omega\phi\,dE_{ij}{\bf b}\qquad\forall\phi\in C^\infty_c(\Omega),\,\,\,i,j=1,\ldots,k.
$$

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{structural}
For any unit vector $\xi$ one has $\langle E{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle=\int_{\pi_\xi} D{\bf b}_{y,\xi}\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y)$, namely
$$
\int\phi(x)\, d\langle E{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle(x)=\int_{\pi_\xi}\int_{\Omega_{y,\xi}}\phi(y+s\xi)\,dD{\bf b}_{y,\xi}(s)\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y)
$$
for any bounded Borel function $\phi$ with compact support. Analogously, 
$$
\langle E^a{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle=\int_{\pi_\xi} D^a{\bf b}_{y,\xi}\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y), 
\qquad
|\langle E^a{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle|=\int_{\pi_\xi} |D^a{\bf b}_{y,\xi}|\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y),
$$
$$
\langle E^s{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle=\int_{\pi_\xi} D^s{\bf b}_{y,\xi}\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y),
\qquad
|\langle E^s{\bf b}\xi,\xi\rangle|=\int_{\pi_\xi} |D^s{\bf b}_{y,\xi}|\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y).
$$
Finally, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sliceJ1}
\int_{\pi_\xi}{\mathscr H}^{0}\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits J_{{\bf b}_{y,\xi}}\,d{\mathscr H}^{k-1}(y)\leq{\mathscr H}^{k-1}\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits J_{{\bf b}}
\end{equation}

label: thm:disinte
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:disinte}
Let $X$, $\mathcal A$ be Polish topological spaces, let $\mathcal F$ be a $\sigma$-algebra containing ${\mathscr B}(\mathcal A)$ 
and let $f:X\to\mathcal A$ be a (${\mathscr B}(X)-\mathcal F$)-measurable map. \\
Then, for every nonnegative and $\sigma$-finite measure $\mu$ in $X$  such that $f_\#\mu$ is $\sigma$-finite
there exist a weakly$^*$ measurable family of measures $\mu_a\in {\mathscr M}_+\bigl(X\bigr)$, $a\in\mathcal A$ , concentrated on $f^{-1}(a)$ 
and unique up to sets of negligible $f_\#\mu$-measure, such that
$\mu=\int_{{\mathcal A}}\mu_a\,df_\#\mu$,
namely 
$$
\int_X\phi(x)\,d\mu(x)=\int_{{\mathcal A}}\int_X\phi(x)\,d\mu_a(x)\,d f_\#\mu(a)
$$
for any Borel function $\phi:X\to [0,\infty]$.

label: thm:Kellerer
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Kellerer}
Let $X$, $Y$ be Polish spaces and $\mu_X\in{\mathscr P}\bigl(X\bigr)$, $\mu_Y\in{\mathscr P}\bigl(Y\bigr)$. Let $C\subseteq X\times Y$ be a Borel set. Then
$$
\sup\left\{\Sigma(C):\ \Sigma\in\Gamma(\mu_X,\mu_Y)\right\}=\min\biggl\{\mu_X(A)+\mu_Y(B):\ {\bf 1}_A(x)+{\bf 1}_B(y)\geq {\bf 1}_C(x,y)\biggr\},
$$
where $\Gamma(\mu_X,\mu_Y)$ consists of all $\Sigma\in{\mathscr P}\bigl(X\times Y\bigr)$ having $\mu_X$ and $\mu_Y$ as marginals, while
the minimization in the right hand side is among all Borel sets $A\subseteq X$, $B\subseteq Y$.

title: Remark
body_md:
{\rm  A beautiful example in \cite{Pap_2025} shows somehow the necessity to deal with {\it generalized} flows in the absence of sufficient smoothness: for any
 integer $k\geq 1$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ a divergence-free vector field ${\bf b}\in C^k_t(C^{0,\alpha}_x)$ is built such that there is no measure-preserving
 selection of characteristics. In this case the superposition principle obviously grants existence of a GRLF, even a measure-preserving one 
 as in Brenier-Schnirelman's theory of generalized incompressible Euler equations (see for instance \cite{AF} and the references therein). 
 More generally, as suggested by the author, without smoothness
 assumptions it is not clear if existence of a RLF for a divergence-free vector field implies that the RLF is measure-preserving.
 
 Still in connection with the impossibility to provide well-behaved selections of characteristics, the well-known example \cite{Depauw_03} of a bounded, divergence-free vector field in $L^1_{\rm loc}\bigl((0,1];BV(\mathbb{T}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)\bigr)$ for which forward uniqueness of \eqref{eq:CE} fails even in the class $\mathcal R_+$
 has been revisited in \cite{Pit_2024}, proving existence and uniqueness of the corresponding GRLF ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$. This GRLF, due to an instantaneous branching at $t=0$, does not have any RLF counterpart, namely a selection of trajectories, indeed the failure of forward uniqueness of \eqref{eq:CE} corresponds to the conditional
 probabilities ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_x$ not being Dirac masses.
}
head: environment

label: rem:invariant
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:invariant}{\rm
The bounded compression condition is useful to show that the notions of RLF and GRLF are invariant in the Lebesgue
equivalence class of ${\bf b}$. Indeed, if $\tilde{{\bf b}}$ is a modification of ${\bf b}$ in a ${\mathscr L}^{d+1}$-negligible Borel set $M$, we know
that for ${\mathscr L}^{1}$-a.e. $t\in (0,T)$ the set $\{\gamma:\ (t,\gamma(t))\in M\}$ is ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-negligible, to be precise, for all $t\in (0,T)$
such that the $t$-section $M_t$ of $M$ is ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-negligible. Then, Fubini's theorem gives that for ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. $\gamma$
the curve $\gamma(t)$ belongs to $M_t$ for a ${\mathscr L}^{1}$-negligible set of times, whence the invariance of condition (i) follows.}
head: environment
name: Invariance of RLF and GRLF in the Lebesgue equivalence class

title: Remark
body_md:
{\rm In order to have an axiomatization of flows invariant under modifications ${\bf b}$ in ${\mathscr L}^{d+1}$-negligible sets, the
$L^\infty$ bound could be simply replaced by a non-quantitative bound $\mathbb{X}(t,\cdot)_\#{\mathscr L}^{d}\ll{\mathscr L}^{d}$ for
all (or even ${\mathscr L}^{1}$-almost all) $t\in (0,T)$, see the argument in Remark~\ref{rem:invariant}. In this connection, on the Eulerian side, in the last few years,
in the class of Sobolev vector fields, many efforts have been devoted to the search of the optimal range of exponents $(p,q)$ (with
$q$ local summability of $\nabla {\bf b}_t$, $p$ local summability of $\rho_t$) ensuring local well
posedness of \eqref{eq:CE}. As soon as $\frac 1p +\frac 1 q<1+\frac 1{dp}$, well posedness in the
class of nonnegative $\rho$'s is ensured by \cite{BCD_2021}, and it is an open problem for signed solutions
(the restriction to nonnegative solutions
comes from the use of the superposition principle, Theorem~\ref{thm:superpo}); on the other hand, the counterexamples built in \cite{BCK}
(see also \cite{MoSa_2020}) show that when $\frac 1p +\frac 1 q>1+\frac 1{dp}$ uniqueness fails.

At the abstract level, it would be interesting to explore a different axiomatization of RLF and GRLF with a quantitative $L^q$ condition,
$q<\infty$, on the time marginals (the main difficulty is due to the fact that $L^q$ bounds on the flow map are not stable under
composition).
}

title: Remark
body_md:
{\rm Existence of a RLF yields existence of a GRLF, simply setting $\eta_x=\delta_{\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)}$.  
On the other hand, existence of a GRLF is equivalent to the existence of nonnegative solutions with $\rho_t$ to \eqref{eq:CE}  
starting from any nonnegative $\rho_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $\|\rho_t\|_\infty\leq C\|\rho_0\|_\infty$ for some $C$
independent of $\rho_0$: indeed, in one direction it suffices to define $\rho_t$ as density of push forward measures, namely
$$
\rho_t{\mathscr L}^{d}=({\sf ev}_t)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\sigma$}}\qquad t\in [0,T],
$$
with ${\mbox{\boldmath$\sigma$}}=\int \rho_0(x)\eta_x\,d{\mathscr L}^{d}(x)=\rho_0\circ{\sf ev}_0\,{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$. Conversely, if we take $\rho^R_0={\bf 1}_{B_R(0)}$, the superposition principle grants
${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}^R$ satisfying \eqref{eq:Lag1}, so that $({\sf ev}_t)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}^R\leq C{\mathscr L}^{d}$ with $C$ independent of $R$; then, a compactness argument based on the growth condition \eqref{eq:growth} grants the existence
of a $\sigma$-finite positive measure ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ in $C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$, finite on all sets $\{\gamma:\ \gamma(0)\in B_R(0)\}$ and concentrated on
absolutely continuous solutions to the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE}, with the
property that $({\sf ev}_t)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}\leq C{\mathscr L}^{d}$ for all $t\in [0,T]$. Then, the conditional probability measures ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_x$ provide a GRLF ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ with
$C({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}})\leq C$. We omit the details, as this implication will not be used in the paper.
}

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$(a)\Rightarrow(b)$. Since any solution $\rho_t$ in this class has a representation \eqref{eq:Lag1} via the superposition principle, it suffices to
check that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\sigma$}}$ is uniquely determined by ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$. Indeed, we can represent ${\mbox{\boldmath$\sigma$}}$ as $\int\rho_0(x)\sigma_x\,d{\mathscr L}^{d}(x)$, with $\sigma_x$ concentrated
probability measures on absolutely continuous solutions to the ODE \eqref{eq:ODE} starting at $x$. As $\|\rho_t\|_\infty$ is uniformly bounded, one also has
$({\sf ev}_t)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\sigma$}}\leq C{\mathscr L}^{d}$ for all $t\in [0,T]$. Now, assume by contradiction that $\sigma_x\neq\eta_x$ in a set with positive $\rho_0{\mathscr L}^{d}$-measure, 
so that there exists $\tau>0$ such that ${\mathscr L}^{d}(F_\tau)>0$, with
$$
F_\tau=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: \rho_0(x)\geq\tau,\,\,\sigma_x\neq\eta_x\}.
$$
If we define
$$
\tilde\eta_x:=
\begin{cases}
\eta_x & \text{if $x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus F_\tau$};
\\
\sigma_x & \text{if $x\in F_\tau$}
\end{cases}
$$
we obtain a different GRLF $\tilde\eta$ with $C(\tilde{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}})\leq C({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}})+C/\tau$, a contradiction. This proves uniqueness of ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$
and the representation of solutions to \eqref{eq:CE} in (ii). 
\smallskip
 
$(b)\Rightarrow(a)$. See Theorem~5.4 of \cite{Am_2004} (or Theorem~3.10 of \cite{AmCri_2014}). The strategy of the proof is to show that any GRLF $\eta_x$ is a Dirac
mass for ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ (thus proving (i) as well), arguing by contradiction and, in particular, using the set of points $x$ where this is not the case to build two
distinct solutions to \eqref{eq:CE} in the class $\mathcal R_+$ and with the same initial condition.

\smallskip

Now, let us prove (iii). Since $\eta_x=\delta_{\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)}$ for ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, it suffices to show the existence of a 
 ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-negligible Borel set $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the family of curves $\{\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\mathcal N}$ 
is forward nonbranching. Let now $\mu_d$ be the standard Gaussian in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or any other probability measure mutually absolutely 
continuous with ${\mathscr L}^{d}$); it suffices to show the existence for
any $\epsilon>0$ of a Borel set $\mathcal N_\epsilon\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ such that  $\mu_d(\mathcal N_\epsilon)<2\epsilon$ and such that
the family of curves $\{\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\mathcal N_\epsilon}$ is forward nonbranching, as the $\mu_d$-negligible set
$\mathcal N=\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mathcal N_{2^{-k}}$ gives the result.

Now, fix $\epsilon>0$ and a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\mu_d(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus K)<\epsilon$ and
$x\mapsto\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ is continuous. Following a strategy similar to \cite{Bia_Bo_2020}, we will apply Theorem~\ref{thm:Kellerer} with $X=Y=\mathbb{R}^d$, $\mu_X=\mu_Y=\mu_d$ 
and
$$
C=\left\{(x,y)\in K\times K: (\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x),\mathbb{X}(\cdot,y))\in G\right\},
$$
where $G$ is the forward branching set in \eqref{eq:fwd_branching}.
Thanks to Lemma~\ref{lem:Borel} and the continuity of $x\mapsto\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ on $K$, $C$ is a Borel set. The ``switching'' operator
$$
{\sf Sw}(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)(s):=
\begin{cases}
\gamma(s) &\text{if $s\in [0,t_{(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)}]$};\cr\cr
\tilde\gamma(s) &\text{if $s\in [t_{(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)},T]$},
\end{cases}
$$
where $t_{(\gamma,\tilde{\gamma})}>0$ is the first time of intersection, is well defined on $G$ and
maps $(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)$ to a curve ${\sf Sw}(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)\neq\gamma$. 

Theorem~\ref{thm:Kellerer} and \eqref{eq:Ketterer1} grant that
either there exists $\Sigma\in{\mathscr P}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\bigr)$ having $\mu_d$ as marginals with $\Sigma(C)>\epsilon$, or there exist Borel sets $A,\,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$
with $\mu_d(A)+\mu_d(B)>2-\epsilon$ and $(A\times B)\cap C=\emptyset$. If the second possibility occurs, we may take
$\mathcal N_\epsilon=\mathbb{R}^d\setminus (K\cap A\cap B)$, as
$$
\mu_d(A\cap B)\geq\mu_d(A)+\mu_d(B)-\mu_d(A\cup B)>1-\epsilon.
$$
To conclude the proof, it suffices to show that the first possibility does not occur. If such $\Sigma$ exists, write $\hat{\Sigma}={\bf 1}_C\Sigma$
and $\hat{\Sigma}=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\hat{\Sigma}_x\,d\mu(x)$, with $\mu=\rho{\mathscr L}^{d}$, the marginal of $\hat{\Sigma}$ with respect to the first factor
and $\hat{\Sigma}_x\in{\mathscr P}\bigl(K\bigr)$. As $\mu(\mathbb{R}^d)=\Sigma(C)>0$, we have 
${\mathscr L}^{d}(F_\tau)>0$ for some $\tau>0$, with $F_\tau=\{\rho>\tau\}$. Now, we may replace $\eta_x=\delta_{\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)}$ by 
$$
\tilde\eta_x:=
\begin{cases}
{\sf Sw}(\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x),\mathbb{X}(\cdot,y))_\#\hat{\Sigma}_x &\text{if $x\in F_\tau$;}\cr\cr
\eta_x & \text{if $x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus F_\tau$.}
\end{cases}
$$
It is clear that $\tilde\eta_x\neq\eta_x$, as ${\mathscr L}^{d}(F_\tau)>0$ and 
${\sf Sw}(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)\neq\gamma$ whenever $(\gamma,\tilde{\gamma})\in G$.
It is not difficult to show that still $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ has bounded compression, whence the contradiction. 

Let us prove, indeed, that $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ has bounded compression; for any Borel set $E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ and any $t\in [0,T]$
we can estimate from above 
$$
\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}\bigl(\{\gamma:\ \gamma(t)\in E\}\bigr)\leq C({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}){\mathscr L}^{d}(E)+
\int_{F_\tau}\hat{\Sigma}_x\bigl(\{y:\ {\sf Sw}(\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x),\mathbb{X}(\cdot,y))(t)\in E\}\bigr)\,dx.
$$
By the very definition of ${\sf Sw}$, the second addendum in the right hand side can be estimated from above by
\begin{equation}
{\mathscr L}^{d}\bigl(\{x\in F_\tau:\ \mathbb{X}(t,x)\in E\}\bigr)+\int_{F_\tau}\hat{\Sigma}_x\bigl(\{y:\ \mathbb{X}(t,y)\in E\}\bigr)\,dx.
\end{equation}
The first term can be estimated once more with $C({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}){\mathscr L}^{d}(E)$; the second term, recalling that
$\mu_d\leq C_d{\mathscr L}^{d}$ and $\hat{\Sigma}\leq\Sigma$, by
$$
\frac{1}{\tau}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\hat{\Sigma}_x\bigl(\{y:\ \mathbb{X}(t,y)\in E\}\bigr)\,d\mu_d(x)\leq
\frac{1}{\tau}\mu_d(\{y:\mathbb{X}(t,y)\in E\})\leq\frac{C_d}{\tau}C({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}){\mathscr L}^{d}(E),
$$
concluding the proof.

title: Remark
body_md:
{\rm 
It would be interesting to know to what extent the equivalence between (a) and (b) in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} can be sharpened. For instance, what are the implications
at the level of the continuity equation \eqref{eq:CE} if we only assume existence and uniqueness of the RLF, not assuming anything on the GRLF? While
existence in the class ${\mathcal R}$ is obvious, the superposition principle of Theorem~\ref{thm:superpo} does not seem to be sufficient to grant uniqueness, even
in ${\mathcal R}_+$, this is an open question. In this connection, in \cite{Bo_Gu}, a bounded vector field ${\bf b}$ is built in one space dimension
whose characteristics are constant: for this vector field existence and uniqueness even of the GRLF are trivial, as well as existence and uniqueness of 
nonnegative measure-valued solutions and solutions in the class ${\mathcal R}_+$ (namely, the constant ones), while uniqueness is proved to fail for measure-valued solutions.  It would be interesting to know if uniqueness for \eqref{eq:CE} might fail even in the class ${\mathcal R}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Statements (a) and (b) are an immediate consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. In order to prove (c), if
we call $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}=\int\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_y\,d{\mathscr L}^{d}(y)$ the unique GRLF relative to $\tilde{\bf b}$, it is clear that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'=j_\#\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ yields a solution of \eqref{eq:CE} with vector field ${\bf b}$,
where 
$$
j:C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)\to C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)\quad\text{is the time inversion, $j(\gamma)(t):=\gamma(T-t)$},
$$
as the bounded compression property at any time $t\in [0,T]$ and the property of being concentrated on solutions are preserved by this transformation.
In particular ${{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}}'=\tilde\rho_T\mathcal{L}^{d}(y)\otimes{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}}_y$, where ${\sf ev}_{T\#}\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}=\tilde\rho_T\mathcal{L}^{d}$.
This implies that for ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-a.e. $y$ the measure $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_y$ is concentrated on
the curves $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ such that $y=\mathbb{X}(T,x)$, as ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on this family of curves.  Since, in addition, 
$\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_y=\delta_{\mathbb{Y}(\cdot,y)}$ has to be a Dirac mass for ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-a.e. $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, 
we obtain the existence of a Borel set $Y_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ of full ${\mathscr L}^{d}$-measure such that for all $y\in Y_0$ there
exists only one $x(y)$ such that $y=\mathbb{X}(T,x(y))$ and more generally $\mathbb{Y}(T-t,y)=\mathbb{X}(t,x(y))$ for all $t\in [0,T]$.  

As $x(y)=\mathbb{Y}(T,y)$, $y\in Y_0$, thanks to Lusin's theorem (applied for instance with the finite reference measure $\gamma_d$, mutually absolutely
continuous with ${\mathscr L}^{d}$)
we can assume with no loss of generality that $Y_0$ is the union of compact sets $K_i$ such that $\mathbb{Y}(T,\cdot)$ is 
continuous on $K_i$; it follows that $X_0=\mathbb{Y}(T,Y_0)$ is a Borel set. Now we can prove that ${\mathscr L}^{d}\ll \mathbb{X}(T,\cdot)_\#{\mathscr L}^{d}$,
more precisely $\mathbb{X}(T,\cdot)_\#{\mathscr L}^{d}\geq (C(\tilde{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}}))^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{d}$. Indeed, for any compact set $E\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one has
\begin{eqnarray*}
{\mathscr L}^{d}\bigl(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\ \mathbb{X}(T,x)\in E\}\bigr)&\geq& {\mathscr L}^{d}\bigl(\{x\in X_0:\ \mathbb{X}(T,x)\in E\}\bigr)\\
&=&{\mathscr L}^{d}\bigl(\mathbb{Y}(T,\cdot)(Y_0\cap E)\bigr)\\
&\geq&\frac 1{C(\tilde{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}})}{\mathscr L}^{d}\bigl(\{y:\ \mathbb{Y}(T,y)\in\mathbb{Y}(T,\cdot)(Y_0\cap E)\}\bigr)\\&\geq&\frac 1{C(\tilde{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}})}{\mathscr L}^{d}(Y_0\cap E)\bigr)
=\frac 1{C(\tilde{{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}})}{\mathscr L}^{d}(E).
\end{eqnarray*}
Eventually, by repeating the argument symmetrically, we may take as $\mathcal N$ the union $\mathcal N_1\cup\mathcal N_2$, where $\mathcal N_1$ and $\mathcal N_2$ are
the Lebesgue negligible sets associated to $\mathbb{X}$ and $\mathbb{Y}$ respectively.

label: eq:decompositionmasscyclicacyclicm
title: Proof
body_md:
In this proof we shall follow the language and notation of \cite{ARV}.
The 1-current  $S=\rho{\bf B}{\mathscr L}^{d+1}$ has locally finite mass, furthermore $\partial S\in{\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$, which means that $S$ is a locally normal current. By \cite[Theorem 1.4]{ARV} it is possible to decompose the 1-current $S$ as the sum of a cyclic current $S_c$
and an acyclic current $S_a$ in such a way that 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:decompositionmasscyclicacyclicm}
        \rho|{\bf B}|{\mathscr L}^{d+1}=\|S\|=\|S_a\|+\|S_c\|,
    \end{equation}
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the mass measure of a current. From \eqref{eq:decompositionmasscyclicacyclicm} we obtain that there exist 
$\rho_a , \rho_c \in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$ nonnegative such that $\rho=\rho_a + \rho_c$, $S_a =\rho_a {\bf B}$ and $S_c =\rho_c {\bf B}$.
Next we show that $S$ is acyclic or, equivalently, that  $\rho_c=0$. 
    
Indeed, since $S_c$ is a cycle, one has $D\cdot(\rho_c{\bf B})=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$,
hence $\rho_c$ is a nonnegative solution of the continuity equation with initial datum 0.
In particular by \eqref{eq:weak1} we obtain 
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi\rho_{c,t}\,dx=\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}{\bf b}_\tau\cdot\nabla\phi\rho_{c,\tau}\,dx\, d\tau
\quad\text{for all $\phi\in C^1_c(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $ t\geq0$.}$$
Fix $r>0$ and consider for $R\geq r$, $\phi_R\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that $0\leq\phi_R\leq 1$, $\phi_R\mid_{B_R(0)}= 1$ and 
$(1+|x|)|\nabla\phi_R(x)|\leq C$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ for some fixed constant $C>0$ independent of $R$. These conditions grant, for all $t>0$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
\int_{B_r (0)}\rho_{c,t}\,dx&\leq&\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi_R\,\rho_{c,t}\,dx\leq
\int_0^t\biggl|\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}{\bf b}_s\cdot\nabla\phi_R\rho_{c,s}\,dx\biggr|\,ds\\
&\leq& C\|\rho\|_\infty\int_0^T \int_{\{\phi_R<1\}} \frac{|{\bf b}^1_s|}{1+|x|}\,dx\,ds+
C\int_0^T \|\frac{|{\bf b}^2_s|}{1+|x|}\|_\infty\int_{\{\phi_R<1\}} \rho_s\,dx\,ds,
\end{eqnarray*}
with the last term going to 0 as $R\to\infty$ by dominated convergence, implying that $\rho_c =0$.
We can then apply \cite[Theorem 1.4]{ARV} and find 
a positive Borel measure ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ over the space $\Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$ of the open ended curves $\sigma(s)$ with 
locally finite length in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ (namely their intersection with any bounded set of $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ has finite length)
such that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-almost every curve $\sigma$ is injective and
\begin{align}
&S=\int_{\Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})} S_\sigma d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\sigma), \label{decomp} \\
&\|S\|=\int_{\Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})} \|S_\sigma\| d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\sigma),\label{masseq}\\
&\partial S=\int_{\Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})} \partial S_\sigma d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\sigma), \label{eq:ARVboundary}\\
& \|\partial S\|=\int_{\Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})} \|\partial S_\sigma\| d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\sigma).\label{eq:ARVvariationboundaryeq} 
\end{align}
where $S_\sigma$ denotes the current with locally finite mass in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ canonically induced by $\sigma\in \Gamma(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$.
Testing $S$ against $\varphi\frac{{\bf B}}{|{\bf B}|}$ for any $\varphi\in C_c(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$ nonnegative, it is possible to show that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. curve $\sigma$ has the property that $\sigma'(s)$ is a nonnegative multiple of $\rho{\bf B}(\sigma(s))=\rho(\sigma(s))(1,{\bf b}(\sigma(s))$ and $\rho(\sigma(s))>0$ for ${\mathscr L}^{1}$-a.e. $s$ such that $|\sigma'(s)|>0$ (see for instance \cite{PhdBonicatto}).
Hence, up to a reparametrization, ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-almost every curve $\sigma$ can be represented as $(t,\gamma(t))$, with $\gamma$ a solution of \eqref{eq:ODE} in an interval $(t_\gamma^- ,t_\gamma^+)\subseteq \mathcal{I}$. 

From now on, with a slight abuse, we will see ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ as a measure
on the curves $\gamma$, noticing that $S_\sigma=S_{(t,\gamma)}$. The fact that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on curves of locally finite length
in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ implies that, for ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. curve $\gamma$, the possibly infinite limits $|\gamma(t_\gamma^+)| := \lim_{t \uparrow t_\gamma^+} |\gamma(t)| \quad \text{and} \quad |\gamma(t_\gamma^-)| := \lim_{t \downarrow t_\gamma^-} |\gamma(t)|$
exist.

Finally, we check that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is indeed concentrated on curves of finite length.
Testing $S$ against $\frac{1}{|{\bf b}|(1+|x|)}(0,{\bf b})$, with $\tau_\gamma=(t_\gamma^++t_\gamma^-)/2$ we find 
\begin{align}
&\int\left|\log\left(\frac{1+|\gamma(t_\gamma^{\pm})|}{1+|\gamma(\tau_\gamma)|}\right)\right|\,d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\gamma)\leq\int\int_{t^-_{\gamma}}^{t^+_{\gamma}} \frac{|\dot\gamma(s)|}{1+|\gamma(s)|}ds\,d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\gamma)=\int\int_{t^-_{\gamma}}^{t^+_{\gamma}} \frac{|{\bf b}(\gamma(s))|}
{(1+|\gamma(s)|)}ds\,d{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(\gamma)\nonumber \\
&= S\left(\frac{1}{|{\bf b}|(1+|x|)}(0,{\bf b})\right)\leq
\|\rho\|_\infty \left\|\frac{|{\bf b}^1|}{1+|x|}\right\|_{L^1((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)}+\int_0^T\left\|\frac{|{\bf b}^2_s|}{1+|x|}\right\|_\infty\int\rho_s\,dx ds
<\infty.
\end{align}
It follows that the first integral is finite, hence ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on curves of finite length.
We conclude by noting that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is a Lagrangian representation.
Indeed since ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is supported on curves of finite length, \eqref{rhoBBrep} follows from \eqref{decomp} whereas \eqref{eq:ARVboundary} and \eqref{eq:ARVvariationboundaryeq} written in terms of $\gamma$ yield \eqref{eq:concancellazioni} and \eqref{eq:nocancellazioni} respectively.

label: prop:meas

head: environment
name: Borel measurability of projections

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us write $\Delta=\cup_p \Delta_p$ with $\Delta_p\subseteq \Delta_{p+1}$ compact, $p\geq 0$. Notice that
compactness of $\Delta_p$ grants a positive lower bound on the length of the intervals of curves $\gamma\in\Delta_p$. We denote by ${\bf J}_k$ the operator
associating to a pair $(\gamma,\tilde\gamma)\in\Delta\times\Delta$ with 
intersections of the domains having length larger than $2^{-k}$ the
new curve obtained by gluing the two curves. Since $\Delta$ is untangled, this construction is possible.

We now define recursively $\Delta_p^{(i)}$ as follows: $\Delta_p^{(0)}=\Delta_p$ and $\Delta_p^{(i+1)}$ is
obtained by applying the gluing ${\bf J}_i$ operator to admissible pairs of curves in $\Delta_p^{(i)}$ and $\Delta_p$.
It is not difficult to prove by induction on $i$ that all $\Delta_p^{(i)}$ are compact (here the lower bound on the length
of intersection plays a role), and that the graphs of all curves $\sigma_{[\gamma]}$
are finite or countable unions of graphs of curves in $\bigcup_{p,i}\Delta_p^{(i)}$.

Now, we fix $q$, $N$ with $N>q$ and we consider the map $\pi_{q,N}:\Delta_q\to\Upsilon$ which associates to a curve $\gamma\in \Delta_q$ the
curve whose graph is the union of the graphs of all curves in
$\bigcup_{p,i=0}^N \Delta_p^{(i)}$ containing $\gamma$ as subcurve. 
Thanks to the compactness of the domain and of the class of curves chosen to build $\pi_{q,N}(\gamma)$, this set-valued map is 
upper semicontinuous, hence Borel (see for instance \cite[Theorem II.20 and Corollary III.3]{Castaing}). It is also clear from
the construction that the graphs of $\pi_{q,N}(\gamma)$ are non decreasing with respect to $N$. 

Now, if we view $\pi_{q,N}$ as an $\Upsilon_0$-valued map, it is  Borel as well and it is clear that
$\pi_{q,N}(\gamma)$ converge as $N\to\infty$ to $\pi_\Delta(\gamma)=\sigma_{[\gamma]}$. This proves that the restriction
of the map $\gamma\mapsto \sigma_{[\gamma]}$ to $\Delta_q$ is Borel, and since $q$ is arbitrary we obtain that the map $\pi_\Delta$
is Borel on $\Delta$.

Finally, to prove that the map $P_\Delta$ is Borel we follow a similar argument, considering the $\Upsilon$-valued approximations
\begin{equation}
P_{q,N}:  \bigcup_{\gamma \in \Delta_q} \mathrm{Graph\,}\gamma\mapsto\Upsilon
\end{equation}

which maps $(t,x)\in\mathrm{Graph\,}\gamma$ with $\gamma\in\Delta_q$ to the curve $P_{q,N}(t,x)$ whose
graph is the union of all graphs in $\bigcup_{p,i=0}^N \Delta_p^{(i)}$ 
containing $(t,x)$.
To check that $P_{q,N}$ is Borel it is sufficient to show
(\cite[Theorem~III.2]{Castaing}) that  
$$
P_{q,N}^{-1}\bigl(\{\gamma: \gamma\cap U\neq\emptyset\}\bigr)
$$
is a Borel set for any open set $U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$. This set coincides with $$\mathscr{G}(\Delta_q)\cap\bigcup_{\sigma \in\bigcup_{p,i=0}^N \Delta_p^{(i)}\,\textit{s.t.}\,\mathrm{Graph\,}\sigma\cap U\neq\emptyset}\mathrm{Graph\,}\sigma$$ which is $\sigma$-compact, hence Borel.

label: lemmasubsupports
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmasubsupports}
Let ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ be a Lagrangian representation concentrated on $\Delta\subseteq\Upsilon$, and let $\Delta'\supseteq \Delta$ be a $\sigma$-compact untangled set.
Let $P:\mathscr{G}(\Delta)\to\mathcal A$ and $P':\mathscr{G}(\Delta')\to\mathcal A'$ be the partitions via characteristics induced by $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$, respectively.
Then there exists a measurable map $U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$, defined implicitly ${\bf m}_P$-almost everywhere by the identity
\[
\pi_{P'} = U \circ \pi_P,
\]
such that the preimage $U^{-1}(a')$ is countable for every $a'\in\mathcal A'$, and
\[
U_\# {\bf m}_P = {\bf m}_{P'}.
\]
Furthermore, considering the disintegration ${\bf m}_P={\bf m}_{P'}\otimes p_{a'}$ with $p_{a'}\in {\mathscr P}\bigl(\mathcal A\bigr)$ concentrated on $U^{-1}(a')$, 
one has
    \begin{equation}\label{formuladensitasottoclasse}
        \tilde{w}_{a'} (t)=\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')}\tilde{w}_{a}(t)p_{a'}(\{a\}) \qquad\text{for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-almost every $a'\in \mathcal{A}'$,}
    \end{equation}
    where $I_a\cap I_b=\emptyset$ for $a,\,b\in U^{-1}(a')$ with $a\neq b$, so that
    \begin{equation}\label{disjointdomains}
        \{t\in I_{a'}\,\mid \tilde{w}_{a'}(t)>0\}=\bigcup_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} \{t\in I_a\,\mid \tilde{w}_{a}>0\}.
    \end{equation}
    In particular,  for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-almost every $a'$, if $\tilde{w}_{a'}\vert_{I_{a'}}>0$, then  $U^{-1}(a')$ is a singleton.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\Delta' \supseteq \Delta$, curves in $\Delta$ which are not equivalent with respect to $\pi_\Delta$ might be equivalent with
      respect to $\pi_{\Delta'}$, because of the addition of curves. Hence, to ${\bf m}_{P}$-almost every  $a\in \mathcal{A}$ we may 
      associate $U(a):=a'$ such that $P^{-1}(a) \subseteq (P')^{-1}(a')$.
   
    Noting that for $a,\,b\in U^{-1}(a')$ with $a\neq b$ one has that $P^{-1}(a)$ and $P^{-1}(b)$ are disjoint subcurves of $(P')^{-1}(a')$, it follows that $U^{-1}(a')$ is at most countable. The measurability of $U$ is a consequence of the following fact: for any $\Omega\subseteq \mathcal{A}'$ one has $U^{-1}(\Omega)=P(P'^{-1}(\Omega)\cap \mathcal{G}(\Delta))$
and $(P')^{-1}(\Omega)\cap \mathcal{G}(\Delta)=\bigcup_{a\in U^{-1}(\Omega)}P^{-1}(a)$.  Hence, if $\Omega\in\mathcal F_{\mathcal{A}'}$, 
$P'^{-1}(\Omega)\cap \mathcal{G}(\Delta)$ is a Borel and $P$-saturated set, so that $P(P'^{-1}(\Omega)\cap \mathcal{G}(\Delta))$ is, by definition, an element 
of the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal F_{\mathcal{A}}$. We have 
$$U_\# {\bf m}_P=U_\#(\pi_P)_\# {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}=(\pi_{P'})_\# {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}={\bf m}_{P'}.$$
By disintegration we have ${\bf m}_{P}={\bf m}_{P'}\otimes p_{a'}$ with $p_{a'}\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{A})$ concentrated on
$U^{-1}(a')$ and
$$\rho \mathscr{L}^{d+1} = \int (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_{a'})_\# \biggl(\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\}) w_a  \mathscr{L}^1\biggr) \, d{\bf m}_{P'}(a'),$$
so that the uniqueness of the disintegration of $\rho \mathscr{L}^{d+1}$ with respect to ${\bf m}_{P'}$ gives
     $$w_{a'}(t) =\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\})w_{a}(t) \qquad\text{for ${\mathscr L}^{1}$-a.e. $t\in\mathbb{R}$} $$
    for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-a.e. $a'\in\mathcal{A}'$.
    Formula \eqref{formuladensitasottoclasse} is trivial at points $t\in I_a$ with $U(a)=a'$. At points
    in the intersection $\overline{I}_a\cap\overline{I}_b$ with $a\neq b$ and $U(a)=U(b)=a'$ it
    follows by noting that \eqref{eqpartition2} and \eqref{eqpartition3} imply that
\begin{equation*}
     |\mu| = \int_{\mathcal{\mathcal{A'}}} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_{a'})_\# |\mu_{a'}| \, d{\bf m}_{P'}(a')\leq 
     \int_{\mathcal{\mathcal{A'}}} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_{a'})_\# \sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\})|\mu_{a}| \, d{\bf m}_{P'}(a')=|\mu|,
\end{equation*}
hence 
  \begin{equation*}
         |D w_{a'}|=|\mu_{a'}|=\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\})|\mu_{a}|  =\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\})|D w_{a}|\qquad\text{ for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-a.e. $a'\in\mathcal A'$,}
    \end{equation*}
    which implies
 \begin{equation}\label{eq_goodsumderivatives}
         (D w_{a'})^+ =\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(a')} p_{a'}(\{a\})(D w_{a})^+ \qquad\text{ for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-a.e. $a'\in\mathcal A'$.}
    \end{equation}
 
 Finally, if $\tilde{w}_{a'}\vert_{I_{a'}}>0$ and both \eqref{eq_goodsumderivatives} and \eqref{formuladensitasottoclasse} hold, then $U^{-1}(a')$ is a singleton. Indeed, the addends on the right-hand side of \eqref{formuladensitasottoclasse} have supports with disjoint interiors and \eqref{eq_goodsumderivatives} rules out cancellations of mass of the derivatives at the boundary.

name: Uniqueness of the minimal partition via characteristics

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider two minimal partitions via characteristics $P_1$, $P_2$  and associated Lagrangian representations  ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_1$, ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_2$,
 respectively supported on $\sigma$-compact untangled sets of curves $\Delta_1$, $\Delta_2$. Since in Definition~\ref{defLagRep} the 
 dependence on the measure ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is affine, convex combinations of ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_1$ and ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_2$ are still Lagrangian representations for 
 $\rho{\bf B}$. Hence, with ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}=({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_1+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_2)/2$ we may find a $\sigma$-compact untangled set $\Delta_{12}$ where ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$
 is concentrated. Hence, considering a $\mathcal{G}_\delta$ ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-negligible set $N\supseteq\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2\setminus\Delta_{12}$ 
 we obtain that
 $$\left(\Delta_1 \cup \Delta_2 \right)\setminus N \,\,\,\textrm{is untangled and induces a minimal partition via characteristics for $\rho{\bf B}$.}$$
 Note that, by Lemma~\ref{lem_partizionieinsiemidicurve}, subtracting $N$ will not change the partitions induced by the sets $\Delta_i$, so we may assume, possibly replacing $\Delta_i$ by $\Delta_i\setminus N$, that $\left(\Delta_1 \cup \Delta_2 \right)$ is untangled and that the equivalence relation 
$\pi_{\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2}$ produces a minimal partition via characteristics $P'$.
 Let $U:\mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{A}'$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lemmasubsupports} 
 (with $\Delta=\Delta_1$, $\Delta'=\Delta_1\cup\Delta_2$) be such that $\pi_{P'}=U\circ \pi_{P_1}$.
 Considering as in \eqref{eqpartition1} the disintegrations
 $$\rho \mathscr{L}^{d+1} = \int_{\mathcal{A'}} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_{a'})_\# (w_{a'} \mathscr{L}^1) \, d{\bf m}_{P'}(a'),\quad
 \rho \mathscr{L}^{d+1} = \int_{\mathcal{A}} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_a)_\# (w_a \mathscr{L}^1) \, d{\bf m}_{P_1}(a)$$
by Lemma~\ref{lemmasubsupports} we have that, since $\tilde{w}_{a'}\vert_{I_{a'}}>0$, that 
$U^{-1}(a')=\{a\}$ and $I_a =I_{a'}$ for ${\bf m}_{P'}$-almost every $a'\in \mathcal{A}'$. 
Hence $U$ is a measurable isomorphism from $(\mathcal{A}',{\bf m}_{P'})$ to $(\mathcal{A},{\bf m}_{P_1})$.
 The conclusion then follows by the analogous argument applied to the decomposition induced by $\pi_{\Delta_2}$,
 taking the composition of the measurable isomorphisms.

label: Untangledsupportofunion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Untangledsupportofunion}
Let ${\bf b}$ be such that all Lagrangian representations related to ${\bf b}$ are untangled.
Let $\rho,\rho' \in \mathcal{R}^{\mathcal{I}}_+$ for some bounded open interval $\mathcal{I}$ with $D \cdot (\rho{\bf B}) = \mu \in {\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$ and $D \cdot (\rho'{\bf B}) = \mu' \in {\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$ and let ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}},\,{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'$ be Lagrangian representations for $\rho{\bf B},\,\rho'{\bf B}$ concentrated on Borel sets $\Delta,\,\Delta'\subseteq \Upsilon$ respectively. 
Then $\Delta\cup\Delta'$ is untangled up to a set of negligible $({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}')$-measure.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a countable dense family $\{t_m\}_{m \in \mathbb{N}} \subset \mathcal{I}$
and consider the associated family of intervals $\{\mathcal{I}_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ having these points as endpoints, we write
$\mathcal{I}_n = (t_n^-, t_n^+)$.

Let $T_n := \{ (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+, \gamma) \in \Upsilon : \mathcal{I}_n \subseteq (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+) \}$ and let $R_n : T_n \to \Upsilon$ be defined as $R_n(t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+, \gamma) = (t_n^-, t_n^+, \gamma)$.
Set ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n:=R_{n\#}({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits T_n)$ and  ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'_n:=R_{n\#}({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits T_n)$ respectively concentrated on $R_n(\Delta\cap T_n)$ and $R_n(\Delta'\cap T_n)$. A straightforward verification shows that the densities $\rho_n$ and $\rho'_n$, defined via the identities $\rho_n (t,\cdot) {\mathscr L}^{d} = (e_t)_{\#} {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n$ and $\rho'_n (t,\cdot) {\mathscr L}^{d} = (e_t)_{\#} {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'_n$, satisfy the property that $\mu_n:=D\cdot (\rho_n {\bf B})$ and $\mu_n':=D\cdot (\rho'_n {\bf B})$ belong to
${\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$. Furthermore, the inclusions 
$$
\text{spt}(\mu_n^-) \cup \text{spt}(\mu_n '^-) \subseteq \{t = t_n^+\}\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{spt}(\mu_n^+) \cup \text{spt}(\mu_n'^+) \subseteq \{t = t_n^-\}
 $$ 
 imply that no cancellations occur at the level of the divergence. Consequently, ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n + {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'_n$ constitutes a Lagrangian representation for $\rho_n + \rho'_n$, the assumption on ${\bf b}$ then implies that it has to be untangled. Hence, there exist $\sigma$-compact untangled
 sets $\Delta_n\subseteq\Upsilon$ where ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n'$ is concentrated and with $N_n:=\Upsilon\setminus \Delta_n$ one has
 $({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}} + {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}')(R_n^{-1}(N_n)) =({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}_n')(N_n)= 0$.  It follows that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'$ is concentrated on the set $\Delta\cup \Delta'\setminus\bigcup_n R_n ^{-1} (N_n)$, and since $\bigcup_n T_n=\Upsilon$ one has
 $$
 (\Delta\cup\Delta')\setminus\bigcup_n R_n ^{-1} (N_n)=(\Delta\cup\Delta')\cap\bigcap_n \left(R_n^{-1}(\Delta_n)\cup T_n^c\right).
 $$
 Since each $\Delta_n$ is untangled, it follows that the set 
$\Delta \cup \Delta' \setminus \bigcup_n R_n^{-1}(N_n)$ is also untangled. 
Indeed, suppose by contradiction that there exist two elements 
$(t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+, \gamma)$ and $(t_{\gamma'}'^-, t_{\gamma'}'^+, \gamma') \in 
(\Delta \cup \Delta') \cap \bigcap_n R_n^{-1}(\Delta_n)$ 
which split at a time $\bar{t} \in (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+) \cap (t_{\gamma'}'^-, t_{\gamma'}'^+)$. 
Then, there exists an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that 
$\bar{t} \in \mathcal{I}_n \subseteq (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+) \cap (t_{\gamma'}'^-, t_{\gamma'}'^+)$. 
Consequently, we would have $R_n(t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+, \gamma)$,
$R_n(t_{\gamma'}'^-, t_{\gamma'}'^+, \gamma') \in \Delta_n$. 
This contradicts the fact that $\Delta_n$ is untangled, as these two elements split at $\bar{t}$.

label: BBL1BVexanduniqueness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{BBL1BVexanduniqueness}
Let ${\bf b}$ be such that all Lagrangian representations related to ${\bf b}$ are untangled and let
$\rho \in {\mathcal R}^{\mathcal{I}}_+$ for some bounded open interval $\mathcal{I}$ with $D \cdot (\rho{\bf B}) = \mu \in {\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$. 
Let $P_{min}$ be the minimal partition via characteristics of $\rho{\bf B}$ and let $\rho'$ be nonnegative with 
$\rho'\leq C\rho$ and $D \cdot (\rho'{\bf B}) = \mu' \in {\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$.
Then $P_{min}$ is a partition via characteristics for $\rho'{\bf B}$. In particular, the curves of the minimal partition for $\rho'{\bf B}$ can be assumed to be subcurves of those of $P_{min}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that, by setting $\rho+\rho' =u\rho$, we have $1\leq u\leq C+1$ on $\{\rho> 0\}$.
 Let ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$, ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'$ be untangled Lagrangian representations for $\rho{\bf B}$ and $\rho'{\bf B}$ concentrated on the sets $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$ and
 the induced minimal partitions $P_{min}$, $P'_{min}$, respectively.
 We may then write
$$\rho \mathscr{L}^{d+1} = \int_{\mathcal{A}} (\mathrm{Id},\sigma_a)_\# (w_a \mathscr{L}^1) \, d{\bf m}_{P_{min}}(a),\quad
\rho' \mathscr{L}^{d+1} = \int_{\mathcal{A}'} (\mathrm{Id},\sigma_{a'})_\# (w_a'\mathscr{L}^1) \, d{\bf m}_{P'_{min}}(a').$$
By Proposition~\ref{Untangledsupportofunion}, the set $\Delta \cup \Delta'$ is untangled up to a set of negligible $({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}} + {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}')$-measure,
hence, by Lemma~\ref{lem_partizionieinsiemidicurve}, applied separately on ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ and ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}'$, 
we may assume, without changing notation, that it is an untangled set. Starting from the identity 
$$u\rho{\bf B}{\mathscr L}^{d+1}=\int_\Upsilon(\mathrm{Id}, \gamma)_\#\left((1,\gamma') {\mathscr L}^{1}\right)\,d({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}')(\gamma) $$
taking into account Remark~\ref{eta+eta'} it is then possible to carry out the construction in Section~\ref{sec_parvia},
 producing a minimal partition 
$P''_{min}:\mathscr{G}(\Delta\cup\Delta')\to\mathcal{A}$ induced by $\Delta \cup \Delta'$ such that 
$$u\rho {\mathscr L}^{d+1} = \int_{\mathcal A''} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_c'')_\# (w_c'' {\mathscr L}^{1}) \, d{\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}(c),$$
with ${\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}=(\pi_{P''_{min}})_\#({\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}+{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}')$. Here the function $w''_c$, defined as in \eqref{eq:formulawa},
has finite pointwise variation for ${\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}$-almost every $c\in\mathcal A''$ and hence admits a lower semicontinuous representative
$\tilde{w}_c''$; the minimality of the partition grants that $\tilde{w}_c''>0$ only on an interval $I_c''$. Note that, in general, $P_{\min}''$ is not a partition via characteristics for $u\rho{\bf B}$, although, being the untangled set larger, it is for both $\rho{\bf B}$ and $\rho'{\bf B}$.
Apply now Lemma~\ref{lemmasubsupports} to $\rho{\bf B}$, with $P=P_{min}$ and $P'=P_{min}''$  to find
$U:\mathcal A \to \mathcal A''$ such that $\pi_{P''_{min}}=U\circ \pi_{P_{min}}$, 
and define the measure ${\bf m}_{P''_{min}}=~(\pi_{P''_{min}})_\# {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$.
Since  ${\bf m}_{P''_{min}} \leq {\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}$, we may write  ${\bf m}_{P''_{min}}=k \,{\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}$, with $k\in L^1(\mathcal{A}'', {\bf m}''_{P''_{min}})$ nonnegative. Applying Lemma~\ref{lemmasubsupports} we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\rho {\mathscr L}^{d+1} &= \int_{\mathcal{A}''} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_c'')_\# \sum_{a\in U^{-1}(c)} (p_c(a) w_a{\mathscr L}^{1}) \, d{\bf m}_{P''_{min}}(c) \\
&=  \int_{\mathcal{A}''} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_c'')_\# \left(k(c)\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(c)} p_c(a) w_a  {\mathscr L}^{1}\right) \,d{\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}(c).\end{split}
\end{equation*}
It follows that
$$
\int_{\mathcal{A}''} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_c'')_\# \left(k(c)\sum_{a\in U^{-1}(c)} p_c(a) w_a  {\mathscr L}^{1}\right) \,d{\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}(c)\geq
\frac{1}{C+1}\int_{\mathcal A''} (\mathrm{Id}, \sigma_c'')_\# (w_c'' {\mathscr L}^{1}) \, d{\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}(c),
$$
hence for ${\bf m}''_{P''_{min}}$-almost every $c\in \mathcal A''$ and every $t\in I''_c$
$$0<\frac{1}{C+1}\tilde{w}''_c(t)\leq k(c)\sum_{a\in P^{-1}(c)} p_c(a) \tilde{w}_a(t) $$
which implies by Lemma~\ref{lemmasubsupports} that there exists a single $a\in \mathcal A$ such that $\sigma_a=\sigma''_c$. That is, up to a bijection of $\mathcal{A}$, we have $P_{min}=P_{min}''$, which means that
$P_{min}$ is also a partition via characteristics for $\rho'$.\qedhere

label: uniqueness_rho'
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{uniqueness_rho'}
Let ${\bf b}$ be such that all Lagrangian representations related to ${\bf b}$ are untangled and let
$\rho\in\mathcal{R}^{(0,T)}_+$  such that $D \cdot (\rho{\bf B}) = \mu \in {\mathscr M}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}\bigr)$ 
and
$$
{\rm spt} \, \mu \subseteq \{t=0\} \cup \{t=T\}
$$
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq1unicitasoluzioniCE}
        \mu^+ =\mu\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits\{t=0\},\qquad\qquad \mu^- =-\mu\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits\{t=T\}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,  in the strip $(0,T) \times \mathbb{R}^d$, the function $\rho$ is uniquely determined by 
the inner trace ${\rm Tr}^{{\rm in}}(\rho{\bf B},(1,0))$ on $\Sigma=\{t=0\}=\partial\{t>0\}$.

name: Uniqueness for (CE

label: idTimes
title: Proof
body_md:
Let ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ be a Lagrangian representation of $\rho{\bf B}$. From \eqref{eq:nocancellazioni} we infer
\begin{equation}\label{idTimes}
(0,T)= (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+)
\qquad\text{for ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. $\gamma$,}
\end{equation}
since otherwise $\mu$ would have mass on intermediate times. Then \eqref{eq1unicitasoluzioniCE} follows immediately from 
\eqref{eq:concancellazioni} and \eqref{idTimes}. For any $\rho$ as above, consider $\tilde{\rho}(t,x):=\rho(t,x)+{\bf 1}_{ (-1,0)}(t) \rho_0(x)$, where $\mu^+ =\rho_0 \mathcal{H}^d \mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits _{\{t=0\}}$. Observe that 
\begin{equation}    
D\cdot(\tilde{\rho}{\bf B})=\rho_0\mathcal{H}^d \mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits _{\{t=-1\}}-\mu^-.
\end{equation}
Arguing as before, for any $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$  Lagrangian representation of $\tilde\rho{\bf B}$, it holds
\begin{equation}\label{Eq:dominioprolungamentocurve-1T}
(-1,T)= (t_\gamma^-, t_\gamma^+)
\qquad\text{for $\tilde{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. $\gamma$,}
\end{equation}

Now, let $\rho'$ be any other solution to the continuity equation with the same initial condition, let 
$\bar\rho=\tilde\rho+\tilde\rho'$ and let $P_{min}$ be the unique minimal partition via characteristics of $\bar\rho{\bf B}$ 
induced by an untangled family $\Delta$.
By Theorem~\ref{BBL1BVexanduniqueness}, $P_{min}$ is a partition via characteristics for $\rho{\bf B}$. This implies that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on curves obtained by restricting to the interval of time $(0,T)$ the characteristics  $(\sigma_a)_{a\in\mathcal{A}}$ associated to $P_{min}$, which by \eqref{Eq:dominioprolungamentocurve-1T} are defined on the interval $I_a=(-1,T)$. 
This means, using the notation of Definition~\ref{def:partition_characteristics} for $P_{min}$, that ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on the set
\begin{equation}\label{inclusionspteta'}
    Z:=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\left\{ \sigma_a\vert_{(0,T)} \right\}.
    \end{equation}

    In particular, ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ is concentrated on a disjoint family of curves in $[0,T)$  (here we invoke the untanglement of the set 
    $\Delta$, see Definition~\ref{defuntangled}).
We can now conclude by noting that we can disintegrate ${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ with respect to the evaluation at the time $t=0$ as
$${\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}=\int \delta_{\gamma_x}\,d(e_0)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}(x)$$
where $\gamma_x$ is the unique curve in $Z$ (and there is one, for $(e_0)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$-a.e. $x$), such that $\gamma_x (0)=x$. 
Then, being $\rho_t \mathcal{L}^d=(e_t)_\# {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$ for all $t \in (0,T)$, we have that $\rho$ is uniquely determined by the measure 
$(e_0)_\# {\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}$, which in turn is given by
$$(e_0)_\#{\mbox{\boldmath$\eta$}}={\rm Tr}^{{\rm in}}(\rho{\bf B},(1,0))\mathscr{H}^d\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .5pt depth 0pt
\vrule height .5pt width 6pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits\Sigma,$$
as an easy consequence of \cite[Lemma 5.6]{Bia_Bo_2020} (see also Remark~\ref{rem_negative_times}).
 Since the argument is symmetric, reversing the roles of $\rho$ and $\rho'$ we obtain that $\rho=\rho'$.

label: def1sidednearlyincompressible
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def1sidednearlyincompressible}
A vector field ${\bf b}: (0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying \eqref{eq:growth} is called one-sided nearly incompressible if there exists $\rho\in\mathcal{R}^{(0,T)}_+$, $\rho\not\equiv0$, satisfying
$D\cdot (\rho{\bf B})=0$ in $(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d$. \\
 A function $u\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$ is said to be a $\rho$-weak solution of  the transport equation if
   $$D\cdot (u\rho{\bf B})=0\qquad\text{in $(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d$}.$$

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As $P_{min}$ is a minimal partition for $\rho{\bf B}$, we have $\inf_{J_a}\tilde{w}_a>0$ on any compact sub-interval $J_a$ of $I_a$, thus 
Vol'pert's Chain Rule and the Leibniz formula for the products of locally bounded $BV$ functions (see e.g. \cite[Theorem~3.96, Example~3.97]{AFP_00})
yield that $w_a^{-1} \in BV_{\rm loc}(I_a)$ and $u_a=w_a^{-1}(u_aw_a)\in BV_{\rm loc}(I_a)$ as well.
The formula \eqref{eq:mu_a_h} is then a simple consequence of the chain rule applied to $h(u_a)$ and of the Leibniz rule
applied to $h(u_a)$ and $w_a$.\qedhere

$$
